sections.h2: Office location and what it records
sections.html:
Find the office at 305 W. Cornelius Harnett Blvd, Suite 200, Lillington, NC 27546. It files deeds, mortgages, plats, powers of attorney and UCC paperwork. The register is an elected post, with a vote every two years per G.S. 161-1.

Anyone can view the records, with one exception: military discharges. Harnett split off from Cumberland County in 1855, and the books begin that year. Fires in 1892 and 1894 wiped out many early volumes.

Title searches are off limits to staff. For a chain of title, you or the buyer must hire an attorney or a title company. The index is organized by name, so if all you have is a street address, find the owner in the county GIS viewer first.

The office's posted fee list carries a July 1, 2026 date and tracks G.S. 161-10. An ordinary deed starts at $26.00 and a loan instrument at $64.00. Pages beyond the included count cost $4.00 each.

Harnett County recording charges, schedule dated July 1, 2026
Document or serviceCharge
Deed or other instrument, pages 1 to 15$26.00
Added pages, either type$4.00 each
Mortgage or trust deed, pages 1 to 35$64.00
Satisfaction or cancellationNone
Plat, per page$21.00
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 each after
Extra subsequent-instrument index reference$25.00

Releasing a loan costs nothing to record, so paying off your mortgage at closing adds no recording charge on that side.

The rate is $2.00 per $1,000 of price, the same as $1.00 for each $500 or part of $500. That rate has been in force since August 1, 1991, replacing a 50-cent rate that began in 1968.

Sellers settle this tax ahead of recording. As laid out in G.S. 105-228.30 proceeds are divided between the county's general fund and the state. The county keeps a small allowance and sends the state its half each month.

Have the closing attorney list it on its own seller line of the settlement statement.

sections.h2: When a deed counts as recorded
sections.html:
Recording happens when staff keys the deed into the system. Walk-ins have no set cutoff, but anything that cannot be keyed by 5:00 p.m. waits for the next business day. Electronic submissions stop at 4:45 p.m.

Order of registration sets priority between competing claims. G.S. 47-18 denies any conveyance, option, lease over three years or right of first refusal effect against lien creditors and paying buyers until the instrument is registered in the county where the land lies.

  • E-recording works for every document type, maps and plats included.
  • Maps are accepted only at 24x36 or 18x24 inches.
  • Mail copy requests to the Suite 200 address. For certified copies of land records, contact the office to arrange them.

Make sure the deed matches the record owner's name exactly. Names cannot be added or dropped on a deed already recorded, which means fixing an error takes a brand-new deed. The office advises hiring an attorney unless legal drafting is familiar to you.

  • Look through the grantor index for open deeds of trust, then ask every lender for a payoff figure.
  • When an agent will sign, look for a recorded power of attorney. Healthcare powers are not recorded here.
  • With an inherited house, the estate papers belong at the clerk of court, which also holds divorce files.
  • The Tax Department, Suite 101 of that same building, can give you any unpaid-tax balance.

A separation agreement shows up at this office only if someone recorded it. If you are separating, find out whether one exists and whether it mentions the house.

sections.h2: How do I get copies of records?
sections.html:
You can walk in, mail a request to Suite 200, or search online. Plain copies are $0.25 each.

Searches work best with the exact spelling on the instrument, so try the seller's name, a spouse's name and any former trust or company name. On older chains, remember the 1892 and 1894 fires. A closing attorney may have to start from later instruments.

The office also records assumed business names, at $26.00 on paper or $41.00 filed online, along with UCC fixture filings. Neither affects a house sale unless the property secures a business loan.

In the online record search, use the Advanced tab and enter a map book and page. Maps kept in a plat cabinet follow a different pattern. Type PC# and the cabinet letter in the book field, then put the slide number and its letter in the page field with no space or dash.

For example, Plat Cabinet C, Slide 123-B is entered as PC#C in the book field and 123B in the page field. The office also keeps an index to plats for browsing by hand.

Boundary questions are common on older houses. Ordering a new survey early, if the one on file looks stale, heads off a delay once the buyer's attorney starts asking. A plat recorded here costs $21.00 per page.

sections.h2: Who records the deed after a tax foreclosure sale?
sections.html:
The winning bidder does. After the court confirms a Harnett County tax foreclosure sale, the bidder receives a commissioner's deed. The county's foreclosure page makes recording it with the register the bidder's job, to be done promptly.

Those properties sell as is. Neither the county nor the commissioner gives a warranty, and no sale depends on financing or marketable title. An owner in that spot can redeem before confirmation, or sell to a buyer able to close first, with a deed recorded at this office in the ordinary way.

sections.h2: A seller's checklist for the register's office
sections.html:
Taking things in order keeps closing simple. First, pull the grantor index under your name and list every open deed of trust. Second, request payoff letters from each lender. Third, have the attorney draft the deed with the owner names spelled as they appear in the record. Fourth, confirm the tax balance with the Tax Department upstairs in Suite 101.

On closing day the attorney sends the deed for recording, and the seller's deed tax is settled before it goes in. Aim to submit before the 4:45 p.m. electronic cutoff, so the deed is registered that day and holds its place in line.

For 2020-2024 the county had 49,845 households averaging 2.73 persons. Median gross rent runs $1,112, while mortgaged owners pay a median $1,594 monthly. Roughly 86.8% of residents aged one and over stayed put the year before, and workers average 32.8 minutes of travel to work, which buyers weigh against price.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a Harnett deed?
faqs.a: Expect $26.00 for a deed up to 15 pages, with $4.00 more per extra page. A mortgage runs $64.00 up to 35 pages. The schedule is dated July 1, 2026.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed excise tax in Harnett County?
faqs.a: It falls on the seller and is paid to the register ahead of recording, at $1.00 per $500 of price or value.

faqs.q: Will the register of deeds check my title?
faqs.a: No, state law bars staff from title work. Use an attorney or title company, or search the name-indexed records yourself, with the GIS viewer to match a name to an address.

faqs.q: How late in the day can a deed be recorded?
faqs.a: Paper filings must be keyed by 5:00 p.m., so a long document should arrive earlier. E-recordings close at 4:45 p.m. Later items are recorded the following business day.

faqs.q: Does it cost anything to record a mortgage satisfaction?
faqs.a: No. Satisfactions and cancellations of deeds of trust are free on the schedule. Lenders normally file the release after payoff.
